headline: Load shedding spikes as gas supply drops across Bangladesh
summary: A shortage of LNG cargoes has led to the closure of a major floating terminal, causing power outages to surge to over 2,500 MW by Wednesday evening.
details: Load shedding has increased across the country after a significant drop in gas supply. The floating LNG terminal of Accelerate Energy shut down at 3 PM on Wednesday due to a lack of of LNG cargoes.

The impact was felt immediately in power production. As electricity demand rose after evening, the shortage of gas led to frequent power outages in various parts of Dhaka and rural areas during intense heat.

According to Petrobangla, total gas supply dropped from 228.9 crore cubic feet at noon to 218.9 crore cubic feet by 6 PM on Wednesday. This left a deficit of approximately 161.1 crore cubic feet against a daily demand of 380 crore cubic feet.
Power grid data shows a dramatic increase in load shedding. At 10 AM, the deficit was only 117 MW, but by 7 PM, it surged to 2,530 MW as demand hit 17,345 MW while supply fell to 14,815 MW.
By 9 PM, load shedding remained high at 2,443 MW. Experts warn that unless there is rain to lower the temperature, power outages may continue through Thursday.
caption:
From 117 MW to 2,530 MW in just a few hours. Gas shortages are triggering massive power outages across Bangladesh.

According to Petrobangla, total gas supply dropped from 228.9 crore cubic feet at noon to 218.9 crore cubic feet by 6 PM on Wednesday. This left a deficit of approximately 161.1 crore cubic feet against a daily demand of 380 crore cubic feet.

Power grid data shows a dramatic increase in load shedding. At 10 AM, the deficit was only 117 MW, but by 7 PM, it surged to 2,530 MW as demand hit 17,345 MW while supply fell to 14,815 MW.

By 9 PM, load shedding remained high at 2,443 MW. Experts warn that unless there is rain to lower the temperature, power outages may continue through Thursday.
